principles.sourceReliability: Reliability is multidimensional. Separate provenance/authority, independence, verifiability, timeliness, version integrity and entity/event specificity. A low-truth-confidence source may still have high market-impact potential.
principles.halfLife: No universal event half-life. Separate factual relevance expiry, attention-diffusion decay and price-response persistence; estimate by event class/horizon only after PIT-safe controls.
principles.directExposure: Direct beneficiary/victim requires an evidence-backed causal path from event -> economic primitive -> firm exposure -> financial transmission -> effective timing. Event sign is not trading sign.
principles.indirectExposure: Second-order propagation requires effective-dated economic edges and hop-by-hop mechanism. Sign can persist, attenuate, invert or disappear.
principles.pricedIn: Priced-in state is latent and cannot be inferred from price direction alone or from ex-post outcome. Use an ex-ante evidence vector and preserve UNKNOWN.
principles.crossValidation: Count independent evidence lineages, not URLs. Syndicated copies of one release are one lineage. Validate field-by-field and preserve conflicts/revisions.
principles.sectorPropagation: Peer/sector propagation must distinguish contagion/common-demand information from competitive/substitution effects and from pure price co-movement.

antiInference: Source class is not a bullish/bearish weight.
Primary/official does not mean correction-proof or earliest.
Two outlets quoting one source are not two independent confirmations.
Low-veracity information can still move prices, so truthConfidence and marketImpactPotential are separate.

halfLifeContract.guard: Never assign one fixed exponential decay or fixed half-life to all event classes before OOS evidence.

antiInference: Customer win does not guarantee earnings benefit without volume/margin/capacity timing.
Input cost inflation can help upstream and hurt downstream depending on pass-through.
Competitor bad news can create both contagion and share-shift benefit.
Second-order edges cannot be invented from thematic similarity.

crossValidationContract.conflictRule: Preserve conflicting values and their knownAt/version history until resolved; do not majority-vote URLs.

antiInference: Industry membership alone does not determine sign.
Leader move is not automatically a valid proxy for peer fundamentals.
Event-specific propagation must not double-count D09 sector RS or D10 supply-chain state.

systemFit.system1: Current official ANNOUNCEMENTS storage is date/title level and lacks intraday firstKnown, lineage, novelty, half-life and exposure semantics; use for coarse context only.
systemFit.system2: Architecture L5 already requires evidence timestamp, mechanism, beneficiary/victim map, confidence and half-life/expiry. This contract supplies missing semantics, but general-news canonical source remains SOURCE_NEEDED.
systemFit.reason: No Taiwan point-in-time versioned general-news archive or prospective/OOS evidence yet.

evidence.finding: Public-news moves can drift while no-news extreme moves can reverse; effects stronger in smaller/illiquid stocks.
Stale/reprinted news receives smaller immediate response yet can trigger temporary overreaction/reversal, especially with retail trading.
Correctly identifying relevant news by type/tone materially strengthens news-price relation.
Media access/dissemination changes trading and speed of information incorporation; media is transmission, not merely content.
Competing information load weakens immediate earnings response and strengthens later drift.
Delayed incorporation of aggregate/macro news around earnings announcers can dissipate by about day seven in their setting, illustrating event-specific rather than universal decay.

evidence.source: Cohen & Frazzini 2008 JF; Menzly & Ozbas 2010 JF
evidence.finding: Economically linked customer/supplier firms exhibit delayed cross-predictability consistent with limited attention/segmentation.
Peer earnings announcements can transmit information within industries; strength varies with economic similarity, volatility and bellwether size.
Contagion and competitive effects can offset or reverse peer signs.
Leader-to-peer positive spillover can be excessive and reverse at peers' own earnings, a direct counterexample to permanent same-sign propagation.

evidence.source: Clarke et al. 2020 Information Systems Research; Arcuri et al. 2023 Journal of Economics and Business
evidence.finding: Low-quality/fake information can still attract attention and move prices, so truth confidence and market-impact potential must be separated.
